name: Takerei Norton
story: Takerei Norton’s 2018 Kā Huru Manu account describes the mapping wānanga, archival research and field trips, including the change from printed labels on topographic maps to direct digital mapping.

The Ngāi Tahu Cultural Mapping Project grew from work to make reliable cultural and historical information available to Papatipu Rūnaka during high-country pastoral tenure review. Takerei Norton managed the project through the Ngāi Tahu Archive team, combining marae hui, archives and field verification with progressively more capable GIS and a linked place-name database. A request for a public atlas followed the 2012 Ngāi Tahu Cultural Summit; its approved material was published as Kā Huru Manu in November 2017.

contentSections.title: Documented contribution in 2019
paragraphs: In the PLACE19 programme, Takerei Norton described Kā Huru Manu’s 2017 launch after more than ten years of research with Ngāi Tahu marae communities and kaumātua. His biography records management of the Ngāi Tahu Cultural Mapping Project since 2007 and involvement in organising the first Māori GIS conference in Christchurch in 2009.
